page.layout: Two printed pages on one scan, left and right. Left page: a main text column with a narrow note column in the left margin, and a catchword at the foot of the column. Right page: cut off at the scan edge, with only the first letters of its lines visible.

main_text.p: conspectu aliquos fugisse, succubuisse alios, quosdam fluctuasse; rebellâsse ve-rò vel in hostium castra transfugisse neminem affirmat; licet Imperatorem in Occidente haberent[?] suæ professionis magnanimum, et in ipso Licinii exercitu Christianos Duces præpotentes: utpote Theodorum, spectata fortitudine virum (inquit Nicephorus) Arsacium[?], genere Persam, cuius inter alios confessores præcipue virtus effulsit (inquit Sozomenus) et denique Auxentium, cuius quia Historia memorabilis est, et ad propositum præsens non impertinens, illam ex In verbo, Auxentius.{a}Suida hic adferam.

[Erat hic in palatio Licinii inter subscribas (quos Latini Notarios vocant) illustri loco: in Imperiali autem domo fons aquæ fuit, & super ea fonte Bacchi simulachrum: tum autem vitis ampla, quæ locum eum omnem tegens, multa cum amænitate obumbravit. Hunc cùm Licinius veluti deambulans, Auxentio et multis præterea aliis eum officijs gratia comitantibus venisset, & Botrum ingentem & maturum è palmite pendentem conspexisset: Auxentio ut eum

page.notes: The right page is cut off by the scan edge; only the first one or two letters of each line are visible (eum, vero, tas, sum, Tu, pone, tiur, fum, ait, run, du, in, ftia, ta, m, be, ci, in, q, a, il, p, p, r), so its text cannot be read and is not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "haberent[?]" (the printed form looks like "habercnt"), "Arsacium[?]" (blot over the letters), "eum" as catchword. Printed "Licinij", "alijs" and "fubscribas" were normalised to i/j per the u/v and i/j rule, and "Licinii" was normalised to a vowel i. The printed "ex" before the Suida reference is followed by a superscript "a" in the text.
